author: WP15
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on CNA's offline GamerServices: stub identities, the JSON store, achievements, leaderboards, the Guide dialogs, presence/privileges/profile and the dispatcher hang. Mostly current, but it still roots the store at SDL_GetPrefPath, says only one Guide overlay can be pending, claims presence strings are formatted and overstates the component requirement. The Development internals page and Tutorial 123 already held most mechanics; presence, privileges, profile, the precision example, reader-entry semantics and the per-family status contract were missing and now live on a new deep dive.

sections.heading: Dispatcher, component, and the historical hang

concepts.text: XNA tied GamerServices to Xbox LIVE and FNA leaves the service-dependent paths inert; CNA supplies offline local identities, locally persisted achievements and leaderboards and two Guide dialogs it draws itself, but no authentication, friends, matchmaking or remote account service.
tokens: no authentication, friends, matchmaking or remote account

concepts.text: GamerServices behaviour falls into three categories at the snapshot: local in-memory work, locally persisted state under CNA-defined policy where Xbox LIVE supplied the policy, and inert API shapes with no local source; none is a claim of Xbox LIVE compatibility.

GamerServicesDispatcher::Initialize creates four fixed SignedInGamer identities, 'Stub Gamer' and 'Stub Gamer (1)' to '(3)'; Player One is not a guest, the other three are, and all four report IsSignedInToLive true because it copies the initialised flag.
Gamer::GetFromGamertag, GetPartnerToken and their Begin/End pairs have no local implementation: they throw NotSupportedException.
SignedInGamer::IsFriend always returns false and GetFriends returns an empty FriendCollection; the friend types work as containers but CNA has no source to populate them.
tokens: the friend types work as containers

concepts.text: A Gamer owns a LeaderboardWriter that stores the owning Gamer*; default copy/move copies that pointer, so a gamer moved or copied after construction leaves its writer pointing at the old address: keep gamers at stable (heap) addresses.
XNA's Presence is a get-only property returning a mutable object; CNA adds a CNAEXT non-const getPresenceProperty() overload so C++ code can mutate presence the same way.

The local store lives below StorageDevice::GetStorageRootEXT()/GamerServices with achievements/ and leaderboards/ subdirectories; StorageDevice::SetAppNameEXT therefore relocates both systems together with save files.

Claim that the store root is based on SDL_GetPrefPath: at the snapshot the storage root comes from an environment-variable chain (Android isolated root, XDG_DATA_HOME, LOCALAPPDATA, HOME, working directory) with no SDL involvement.
concepts.note: Not copied; the TARGET chain is documented on the Storage guide and repeated on the GamerServices contract page.

concepts.text: Achievements are one JSON file per sanitised gamertag with {key, earnedTicks} records and leaderboards one file per sanitised (key)_(gameMode); bytes outside letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' become '_' and an empty name becomes '_'.
Store writes go to an adjacent temporary file followed by a rename, with a direct write as fallback when the rename fails; a missing or malformed file reads as an empty store.
tokens: falls back to a direct write

concepts.text: Every JSON number is a double, so ticks, ratings and 64-bit column values lose bits above 2^53; a 2026 DateTime (about 6.39e17 ticks) is quantised to a 128-tick (12.8 microsecond) step; the stored integer is stable after the first save but the original value is not a bit-exact round trip.
concepts.note: IEEE-754 arithmetic over the source; not measured.

concepts.text: GetAchievements returns entries with the persisted Key, IsEarned true and EarnedDateTime; Name and Description are empty, GamerScore 0 and DisplayBeforeEarned true, because Xbox LIVE supplied that catalogue metadata and CNA has none.
Games that display achievement names, descriptions or scores must keep their own catalogue keyed by achievement key.
Achievement::GetPicture() throws NotImplementedException: artwork is service-owned data with no local source.

LeaderboardReader, LeaderboardWriter and LeaderboardEntry are disk-backed with CNA-specific policy, because the FNA code CNA ports from has no functioning PC implementation to inherit sorting or paging from.
Leaderboard entries sort by rating, descending (ties unordered).
Reading a page centred on a pivot gamer who is absent from the board starts at the top.
tokens: start 0 when the pivot is absent

concepts.text: Persisted leaderboard entries whose gamertag matches no currently signed-in Gamer are omitted and take no rank.
tokens: A persisted entry only appears if its gamertag is currently signed in

concepts.text: The leaderboard Begin/End pairs complete synchronously, before Begin returns.
XNA's LeaderboardWriter has no submit method, so assigning Rating on an entry obtained from the writer is the commit: it persists immediately with the entry's current columns.
tokens: There is no submit or commit call

concepts.text: An entry created by LeaderboardReader has no persistence hook: changing its rating changes only the in-memory object, not the file.

Most Guide UI calls are no-ops with empty bodies: ShowComposeMessage, ShowFriendRequest, ShowFriends, both ShowGameInvite overloads, ShowGamerCard, ShowMarketplace, ShowMessages, ShowParty, ShowPartySessions, ShowPlayerReview, ShowPlayers, ShowSignIn, ShowAchievementsEXT, plus DelayNotifications.

BeginShowMessageBox and BeginShowKeyboardInput are real dialogs the game draws: they stay pending until answered, the game calls RenderPendingMessageBoxEXT / RenderPendingKeyboardInputEXT each Draw with a SpriteBatch, SpriteFont and white pixel, the hooks poll input, and Guide.IsVisible reports whether a request is pending (keyboard text itself arrives through TextInputEXT even without the render call).
concepts.note: Nuance added: Enter completes keyboard input via TextInputEXT without the render call; Escape cancel needs it.

concepts.text: Keyboard input keeps UTF-16 surrogate pairs intact; password mode masks each displayed code unit while End returns the unmasked text; Escape cancels.
Because std::string cannot represent XNA's null result for a cancelled keyboard request, callers must query WasKeyboardInputCanceledEXT before interpreting the returned (empty) text.

Claim that only one Guide overlay can be pending: at the snapshot there are two slots, one keyboard request and one message box, each refusing a second request of its own kind, so both kinds can be pending at once.
The Guide test corpus covers pending state, callback identity, Enter and Escape, prompt fields, password display and competing requests.

Historical: an earlier Guide implementation ignored title and description, reported IsVisible false, showed password text unmasked and had no cancel path, while a completed task record overstated the behaviour.
concepts.note: All four are fixed at TARGET: Guide.cpp stores and renders title/description, IsVisible reflects the two pending slots, ComputeDisplayText masks password text, and Escape/SimulateKeyboardInputCancelEXT cancel; GamerServicesServiceTests pins each. Told as history on the GamerServices contract page (#guide).

target.evidence: modules/gamer-services/src/Xna/Guide.cpp (stored Title/Description, getIsVisibleProperty, ComputeDisplayText masking, Escape edge + SimulateKeyboardInputCancelEXT)

concepts.text: Claim that GamerPresence formats parameterised modes: it holds all 60 XNA display strings including {0} templates, but nothing substitutes the value, and the selected string is private and passed only to an empty hook, so only PresenceMode and PresenceValue are observable.
GamerPresence's SetPresenceModeStringEXT publication hook has an empty body: no service consumes presence.
concepts.note: Post-Phase-3 adversarial audit correction: the presence hook description now also says the table is indexed by ordinal although the table is alphabetical (audit finding C10 ch49-F1; CNA-BUG-173).

concepts.text: GamerPrivileges is a fixed, fully permissive value (Everyone / true for every privilege) and nothing in the runtime enforces or consults it.
tokens: Nothing in the runtime consults them

concepts.text: GamerProfile uses synthetic defaults (score 0, zone Pro, reputation 5, one title, no achievements, empty motto, null picture) except the host-derived Region.
Presence, privileges and profile carry useful local state but are neither an authentication source nor a policy authority.
tokens: not an authentication source or a policy authority

concepts.section: Dispatcher, component, and the historical hang
concepts.text: Claim that GamerServicesComponent must be added before using the Gamer or Guide APIs: the component (or a direct GamerServicesDispatcher::Initialize) is what populates the signed-in gamers, while the Guide dialogs and the store do not depend on it.
tokens: The component is what populates the signed-in gamers

concepts.section: Dispatcher, component, and the historical hang
concepts.text: The dispatcher creates and frees the local gamer set; GamerServicesDispatcher::Update() is empty and each local asynchronous implementation completes its own action.

concepts.section: Dispatcher, component, and the historical hang
concepts.text: After Initialize, GamerServicesDispatcher::UpdateAsync() returns true indefinitely; ported polling loops that waited for false (NetworkSession create/find/join, SignedInGamer::GetAchievements) could spin forever.

concepts.section: Dispatcher, component, and the historical hang
concepts.text: CNA performs network create/find/join work synchronously in the matching End* and constructs NetworkSessionAction already completed instead of waiting for an event that cannot occur.

concepts.section: Dispatcher, component, and the historical hang
concepts.text: Because the dispatcher's process-lifetime statics have no reset hook, the initialised dispatcher is exercised by a separate-process harness under a ten-second watchdog, which also checks the four identities, sign-in events, achievement completion and reinitialisation cleanup.

Headers and implementations establish API shapes, identities, file layout, overlay hooks and stubs; unit tests cover persistence and Guide state and the harness the dispatcher; none can establish Xbox LIVE interoperation, for which CNA has no transport.

Status summary: local gamers in memory, achievements and leaderboards locally persisted, presence/privileges/profile synthetic, friends and remote lookup empty or unsupported, most Guide.Show* no-ops, message box and keyboard input CNA-drawn, avatar XNA API inert.

examples.note: g++ -std=c++23 -fsyntax-only against TARGET headers + sibling sharp-runtime headers; comments corrected (presence is stored, not published).

Corrected: completion is tested on the request (getIsCompletedProperty) rather than Guide.IsVisible, which a pending message box would keep true; render call wrapped in SpriteBatch Begin/End; End is called on both outcomes before delete.

issues.text: GamerServicesDispatcher::Update() is a permanent no-op and UpdateAsync() returns true forever after Initialize; any Begin/End pair whose action is not completed at construction would spin in the XNA-idiomatic polling loop.
issues.evidence: modules/gamer-services/src/Xna/GamerServicesDispatcher.cpp (Update empty, UpdateAsync); NetworkSession.cpp, SignedInGamer.cpp, LeaderboardReader.cpp (actions completed at construction); Guide actions pending but no polling wrapper

issues.text: GamerPresence's 60-entry presenceModeStrings_ table is ordered alphabetically by mode name, but setPresenceModeProperty indexes it by the GamerPresenceMode ordinal (None=0 maps to 'Arcade Mode'); the selected string is currently unobservable (private, passed only to the empty SetPresenceModeStringEXT). Whether FNA shares the ordering was not checked.

Achievement earnedTicks, leaderboard ratings and int64 columns are stored as JSON doubles and lose low bits above 2^53 (2026 ticks rounded to 128-tick steps), while LocalGamerServicesStore.hpp documents earned ticks as an exact round trip.
The synchronous LeaderboardReader::Read/PageDown/PageUp wrappers never delete the action their Begin* allocates, unlike GetProfile/GetAchievements, leaking one small object per call.
Fourteen Guide Show* entry points plus DelayNotifications are empty no-ops (no local shell UI for sign-in, friends, marketplace, messages, party, gamer card, achievements).
Achievement catalogue metadata (name, description, gamer score) is never populated and Achievement::GetPicture() throws NotImplementedException.
Presence is never published (empty SetPresenceModeStringEXT) and GamerPrivileges is a fixed permissive constant that nothing enforces; GamerProfile is synthetic except Region.
No online service: no authentication, friends graph, matchmaking or remote account exists; GetFriends is empty and gamertag lookup throws. Architectural decision, not a defect.
